Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Global Insurance Holdings Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Global Insurance Holdings' third quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Claims Officer; and Alex Rivera, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Global Insurance Holdings' performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by favorable changes in actuarial assumptions boosting earnings, consistent net favorable reserve development trends, the positive impact of pricing changes expanding premium volume, manageable total catastrophe losses, the effectiveness of our reinsurance program in recoveries, robust new business production volumes, ongoing share repurchase activity returning capital to shareholders, and solid investment income yields. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

David Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Chen: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $650 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included favorable changes in actuarial assumptions, reserve development trends, pricing impacts on premiums, catastrophe losses, reinsurance effectiveness, new business growth, share repurchases, and investment yields. Our combined ratio was 92.1%. Investment income for the quarter was $285 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 520% RBC. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.5%.

Let me expand on these drivers starting with changes in our actuarial assumptions and their impacts. These updates are based on emerging data, regulatory shifts, and advanced modeling, ensuring reserve adequacy and pricing discipline. For the year to date, we realized a net favorable $285 million pre-tax impact from these changes, accounting for about 12% of our adjusted operating income near $2.4 billion. This reverses a $110 million headwind from last year due to rising rates. By segment, Life and Annuities gained $180 million, Property & Casualty $75 million, and Health $30 million, all approved by our Chief Actuary and compliant with ASOP 41 and VM-21 principles.

In Life and Annuities, representing 45% of reserves at $120 billion, we refined longevity and lapse assumptions post-pandemic. Mortality updates used a 2017 CSO table blended with our COVID experience, showing 2.5% improvement from vaccines and healthcare, releasing $120 million for term and whole life blocks. Lapse rates were 15% below prior estimates, especially in universal life with secondary guarantees, reducing assumptions by 10-20 basis points for another $40 million gain, matching LIMRA's low 4.2% industry lapses. Discount rates dropped 75 basis points to 3.2% due to lower Treasury yields, adding a $25 million offset, but our hedging covering 85% of liabilities via swaps and Treasuries limited volatility. U.S. drove 70% of benefits, Europe under Solvency II saw moderated gains, and Asia-Pacific annuities growth cushioned impacts.

For Property & Casualty with $80 billion reserves, we netted a $75 million release after a prior headwind. Loss trends rose 1.2 points to 5.8% for auto liability amid social inflation and verdicts, but favorable development on 2021-2022 years via AI claims triage—cutting cycle times 22%—released $90 million, aligning with industry auto severity up 8%. Cat modeling with RMS v18 strengthened Florida hurricane reserves by $20 million, offset by California wildfire improvements, while attritional losses ticked up 50 basis points to 58% from repair inflation, eased by 9% premium growth. U.S. commercial lines led releases, UK motor neutral under IFRS 17.

Health's $25 billion Medicare Advantage and group book released $30 million from lower morbidity and utilization, adopting 2024 MGU tables down 3%, with inpatient days 7% below plan and stars ratings at 4.2 supporting 5% membership growth.

These stem from $50 million in actuarial tech like Prophet Enterprise for stochastic projections and ML lapse forecasting up 18% accurate, plus P&C GLMs with telematics. This bolsters our 95.8% combined ratio and 14.2% ROE. Forward, stability assumed barring Fed cuts—sensitivity at $120 million EPS hit—or inflation; we're reinsuring tails at Lloyd's with 30% quota shares.

Next, our reserve development trends showed $285 million net favorable prior accident year development in the quarter, adding 3.2 points to our 92.1% combined ratio—our 15th straight quarter, $1.2 billion year-to-date or 4.5 points. P&C at 72% of premiums delivered $210 million favorable, 3.8 points, from commercial auto $95 million on moderating repairs (actual inflation 6.2% vs. 8-10% assumed) and workers' comp $65 million from return-to-work and telemedicine cutting IBNR 12%. Specialty lines $55 million, D&O $30 million on lower cyber claims, cyber neutral. Personal $20 million from homeowners subrogation.

U.S. 85% at $240 million favorable, Northeast $110 million from weather and 9.2% rates; Southeast $25 million unfavorable from Idalia contained by reinsurance. International $45 million, UK motor $28 million from lower frequency, Europe casualty $17 million.

Drivers include AI Bornhuetter-Ferguson models cutting IBNR error 22%, Claims Accelerator speeding cycles 18% accuracy 94% for $110 million LAE favorable, and reinsurance capping wildfire tails. Unfavorable $85 million gross from liability asbestos and auto parts. Expect $200-250 million Q4 favorable; 5-year average 3.7 points beats industry.

On pricing changes' impact on premium volume, we grew net written premiums 8.7% to $14.2 billion. P&C 72% saw 6.8% earned rate increases, 9.4% renewal boost $650 million; casualty 5.5% rates led to 2.1% volume dip but better selection. Retention 87.5% via Aurora Pricing Engine with telematics and GLMs. U.S. 7.5% rates 10.2% growth; Europe flat rates 3.8% growth with marine wins; Asia 6.3% rates 9.1% expansion. Personal 4.2% rates 12.5% growth via embedded partnerships. Pricing drove 62% growth; target 4-6% rates into 2025.

Total catastrophe losses pre-reinsurance hit $1.42 billion or 2.8% of $50.7 billion GWP, up from 2.3% last year; net $485 million or 1.0% of NEP, keeping ex-cat ratio 92.4%. U.S. $880 million: SCS $620 million, wildfires $160 million, Idalia $100 million. Europe $310 million windstorm/floods. Asia $230 million typhoon/monsoons. Ex-cat loss ratio 58.2%. Reinsurance $2.8 billion tower with cat bonds; trimmed exposures, diversified hubs, parametric triggers. Guide FY net cats $4.2-4.6 billion.

Our reinsurance program proved highly effective, with net ceded $3.2 billion or 25.8% GWP, cost ratio 18.4% improved 120 bps, ceding commissions 28% vs. industry 32%. In $1.8 billion gross cats, recoveries $1.5 billion or 83%, including $950 million XOL from Swiss Re, Munich Re, RenaissanceRe, and $450 million quota-share from Berkshire-led consortium with strong collateral.

New business production hit $3.4 billion APE up 22% YoY, 1.45 million policies up 28%. Life & Health 42% $1.43 billion up 19%, UL/term 25%; P&C 58% $1.97 billion up 24%, commercial 32%. North America 65% up 26%, EMEA 22% offset by UBI, Asia 13% up 18%. Digital UnityNow cut times 60%, new riders like parametric cyber $120 million APE, agent productivity up 18%. Raised FY guidance $12.5-13 billion.

Share repurchases totaled $425 million in Q3 under $4 billion authorization, YTD $1.6 billion, 3.1 million shares at $148.72 average below intrinsic $185, reducing shares 1.8% for 2.1% EPS accretion. Rule 10b5-1 automated 68%, ASR $120 million. U.S. aggressive $285 million, Europe moderated, Asia $55 million. Remaining $2.4 billion, Q4 $450-500 million.

These elements combined for our strong quarter.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced telematics integration and dynamic pricing strategies aligned with loss trends.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. Our investment income yield came in at 4.18% annualized, up 22 basis points sequentially and 58 year-over-year, on $48.7 billion assets yielding $285 million NII. Fixed income 4.45% from corporates/munis, new money 5.1%; equities 6.2%, alternatives 7.8%. U.S. 4.35%, Europe 3.65%, Asia 3.40%. ALM matches durations at 5.8 years, swaps hedge cuts; ESG 28% new bonds. Positioned for 4.1-4.3% Q4.

Emily Vargas: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI triage reducing cycles 22% and accuracy boosts. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times and improved claims resolution rates, contributing to favorable development.

Alex Rivera: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new Aurora Pricing Engine and Claims Accelerator platforms, leveraging ML and cloud tech, are expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings across underwriting and claims.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on reserve development trends?

Michael Reynolds: Thanks, John. David can provide more detail.

David Chen: Absolutely. As I noted, $285 million favorable this quarter across segments, driven by better loss emergence in auto and workers' comp, superior modeling, and claims initiatives—our track record speaks to disciplined practices outperforming peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of catastrophe losses on your business?

David Chen: Good question, Maria. Net impact $485 million or 1% NEP, contained by reinsurance and exposure management; ex-cat trends improving, positioning us well cycle-wise.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Regulatory shifts like Solvency II tweaks are embedded in our models; we're adapting via diversified pricing and reinsurance, maintaining margin targets without volume chase.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platforms?

Alex Rivera: Sure. Platforms like Aurora and Claims Accelerator cut times dramatically, improve accuracy, and enable granular risk selection—already lifting retention and new business while containing costs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Harris with Citigroup.

Tom Harris: Thanks. More on actuarial assumptions—how sustainable?

David Chen: Updates reflect data-driven refinements; stability expected absent macro shocks, with sensitivities tested.

Operator: Our next question from Lisa Chen with UBS.

Lisa Chen: Pricing outlook post-hardening?

Lisa Patel: Continued 4-6% earned rates, leveraging tech for precision amid softening pockets.

Operator: That covers our questions for now.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Global Insurance Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
